title: Fully differential telescopic OTA
description: A fully differential telescopic-cascode OTA. Each side stacks an input device, an NMOS cascode, a PMOS cascode, and a PMOS load between the rails, above a tail device shared by the two sides; the cascodes boost the output resistance so a single stage reaches high gain. $A_v = g_{m,in} * R_{out}$, where each side's output resistance is a cascode-boosted branch resistance combined in parallel: looking down, the NMOS cascode multiplies the input device's $r_o$ by its intrinsic gain ($A_{v0,cascn}/g_{ds,in}$); looking up, the PMOS cascode multiplies the load's $r_o$ ($A_{v0,cascp}/g_{ds,load}$). Those branch expressions are the standard cascode approximation (they drop second-order $g_{mb}$ and finite-cascode-gain terms). Being fully differential, there is no current-mirror in the signal path and therefore no mirror pole or its attendant pole-zero doublet — a real frequency-response advantage over the single-ended mirror-loaded stage. Common-mode feedback is required to set the output common mode, but the CMFB loop itself is out of this sheet's scope (no loop solving): it appears only as a current line item $I_{cmfb}$ added to the supply budget. The differential output swing is twice the single-ended cascoded headroom. Only the tail's bias reference is programmed, with $I_{tail}$: the tail device shares its gate and width and delivers the programmed current less the mirror's drain-voltage error, and each side carries half of what it delivers, so a design held fixed at another process condition follows its reference instead of carrying a typed current. Entered from the COMMON MODE like its siblings: the tail node is solved by a design constraint so the input common mode it produces, the tail node plus the input devices' gate-source voltage, equals $CM_{dc}$. The cascode gates are bias lines drawn with the branches that set them, each a stacked replica bias with its own programmed current: a diode on the rail whose drop places the node under the cascode, and a device at the cascode's inversion level stacked on it, whose gate is the cascode gate. The nodes under the two cascodes, $V_a$ and $V_b$, are solved under those gates by design constraints, so wherever the design is held they move with the devices, as silicon's do; the knobs that place them are the bias branches' inversion levels. The loads' gate is the common-mode feedback loop's, which this sheet does not draw, so it stays a port. The two inputs are held at $CM_{dc}$ and the two outputs at $V_{out}$, the level the output common-mode loop keeps them at. Every device in the stack declares that it must stay saturated. On the demo NMOS table every device sizes against the same data.

params.name: Av_target
params.note: differential DC gain target: 300 (about 50 dB) is what one cascoded stage reaches at these lengths without gain boosting, about 8-bit static accuracy in unity feedback, the class of a switched-capacitor integrator or sample-and-hold of moderate precision. An example, to be replaced with the design's own spec

params.name: swing_target
params.note: required differential peak output swing

params.name: v_margin
params.note: headroom beyond the four stacked cascode vdsat drops (tail saturation plus safety) folded into the swing estimate

params.name: I_cmfb
params.note: current the common-mode feedback network draws; the CMFB loop itself is out of scope (no loop solving here) — this is a supply-budget line item only

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the current the bias reference is programmed to — the one current on this sheet that is typed. The tail device mirrors it 1:1 through the shared gate and delivers it less the mirror's drain-voltage error (the tail node sits below the reference's diode drop); each side carries half of what is delivered, and the supply current is computed from that, not from this number

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion (sets gm_in and input noise)

params.name: gm_id_cascn
params.note: NMOS cascode inversion

params.name: gm_id_cascp
params.note: PMOS cascode inversion

params.name: gm_id_load
params.note: PMOS load inversion

params.name: gm_id_tail
params.note: inversion level of the bias reference, which the tail device inherits through the shared gate: a higher V* costs headroom at the tail node

params.name: gm_id_cbn
params.note: inversion level of the NMOS cascode bias branch's bottom diode, whose drop V_a sits near: a lower gm/ID raises V_a, which gives the input devices more drain voltage and the output less swing. The default puts V_a near 0.52 V on the demo model and 0.58 V on a sky130 tt realization

params.name: L_cbn
params.note: length of both devices of the NMOS cascode bias branch. A long branch sits at a lower gate-source voltage than a half-micron one on a sky130 table, where the threshold falls with length, and a little higher on the demo model, where it rises: at 2 um the two tables place V_a within 60 mV of each other

params.name: I_cbn
params.note: the current the NMOS cascode bias branch is programmed to. A diode at a given inversion level sits at one gate-source voltage whatever its current, so this sets only the branch's widths and its share of the bias power

params.name: gm_id_cbp
params.note: inversion level of the PMOS cascode bias branch's top diode, whose drop below the supply the load's drain, V_b, sits near: a lower gm/ID lowers V_b, which gives the loads more drain voltage and the output less swing. A PMOS threshold on a sky130 table is large, so the diode sits near weak inversion to leave the PMOS cascode room above the output: V_b lands near 1.41 V on the demo model and 1.20 V on a sky130 tt realization with the PMOS devices on the pfet table

params.name: L_cbp
params.note: length of both devices of the PMOS cascode bias branch

params.name: I_cbp
params.note: the current the PMOS cascode bias branch is programmed to; like I_cbn it sets only the branch's widths

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis. This sheet claims no operating range: the input device's drain sits at V_a, which the NMOS cascode bias line places whatever the common mode, so a higher common mode lifts the tail node into it, and range ends would only restate that

params.name: V_s
params.note: the tail node (input-pair source). Solved rather than set: searched between min and max (the range it is searched in, not slider bounds) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. The range stops below V_a, the input devices' drain, as the single-ended telescopic's does. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke, and it is the tail device's drain-source voltage, so it also sets the current the tail delivers

params.name: V_a
params.note: input-device drain / NMOS-cascode source node. Solved, not set: the cascode's gate is the NMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that hangs the cascode's own gate-source voltage under it, near the bias branch's bottom-diode drop; gm_id_cbn is the knob that moves it. Searched between min and max, inside the range the wiring puts the node in; the stored value is never read

params.name: V_out
params.note: output common-mode DC level. A common-mode feedback loop, not drawn on this sheet, holds the outputs here; this is that loop's reference

params.name: V_b
params.note: PMOS-cascode source / load-drain node. Solved, not set: the cascode's gate is the PMOS cascode bias line, so this is the node that sits the cascode's own gate-source voltage above it, near one bias-branch top-diode drop below the supply; gm_id_cbp is the knob that moves it. Searched between min and max, inside the range the wiring puts the node in; the stored value is never read

params.name: p_sign
params.note: vds sign of the PMOS device tables: +1 N-style, -1 signed-PMOS

doc.title: Tail current source
doc.description: The tail device, on the bias reference's gate at the reference's width: a 1:1 mirror of the programmed current, with the tail node $V_s$ as its drain-source voltage. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the reference sits at its own diode drop and this device at the tail node $V_s$, so it delivers the programmed current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. It has to stay saturated, and it leaves saturation when the tail node $V_s$ falls below its own $V_{dsat}$, which sets the floor under the tail node.

params.name: W_t
params.note: the bias reference's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_t
params.note: the bias reference's gate voltage — the gate wire the two share

params.name: vds_t
params.note: the tail node

doc.title: Input pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device, carrying half of what the tail delivers; its gm sets the stage transconductance and its output conductance is the bottom of the down-looking cascode branch.

doc.title: NMOS cascode device
doc.description: The NMOS cascode over the input device; its intrinsic gain multiplies the input device's output resistance (the down-looking branch of Rout).

doc.title: PMOS cascode device
doc.description: The PMOS cascode under the load; its intrinsic gain multiplies the load's output resistance (the up-looking branch of Rout).

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: PMOS load device
doc.description: The PMOS load, in the input device's branch and carrying that device's current; its output conductance is the top of the up-looking cascode branch.

params.name: vx
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; it rises monotonically with the tail node, so the design constraint that places the tail node from CM_dc is a well-posed one-unknown search

equations.name: Rdown
equations.note: down-looking branch resistance: the input device ro boosted by the NMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

equations.name: Rup
equations.note: up-looking branch resistance: the load ro boosted by the PMOS cascode intrinsic gain (cascode approximation)

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: single-side output resistance = the two cascode branches in parallel. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this equation is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: swing_diff
equations.note: differential output swing = twice the single-ended range left after the four stacked cascode vdsat drops and the tail/safety margin

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — what the tail device delivers, plus the CMFB network's budget (the CMFB loop itself is out of scope). The reference branch that programs the tail and the two cascode bias branches are shared bias infrastructure and are not counted here. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: thermal noise density referred to the differential input: both input devices and both PMOS load current sources. A load puts its full noise current into the output, so it is referred to the input by the ratio of its transconductance to the pair's, and it is small only where the load's $g_m$ is kept well below the pair's. The cascodes add little: each is degenerated by the output resistance of the device under it. The tail's noise is common to both sides and cancels at the differential output

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No check reads it

checks.note: single-stage cascoded gain meets the target
the differential output swing meets the target
